vulnerabilities.description: attr before version 2.6.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the getfattr and setfattr utilities that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing a pathname component with a symbolic link during directory hierarchy traversal. Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect getfattr and setfattr operations to arbitrary files by substituting a symlink, leading to local privilege escalation when getfattr or setfattr is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The Liquibase Secure image does not ship the getfattr or setfattr utilities.

ratings.justification: The getfattr and setfattr utilities that carry the vulnerable code are not installed in the Liquibase Secure image.

analysis.detail: Scanner package misattribution. The vulnerable code is the getfattr and setfattr utilities, which Ubuntu ships in the separate attr binary package. attr is not installed in the Liquibase Secure image: dpkg lists only libattr1 (the libattr.so.1 shared library used by coreutils such as cp and mv), and there is no getfattr or setfattr binary on the image. The scanner matched a fix in the attr source package to libattr1, which does not contain the vulnerable code.
